title: Graduate Engineer - Contracts
abstract: Turn your engineering potential into real-world outcomes.
bullets: Work on real projects that shape your future.
content_text:
City of Newcastle is fortunate to be able to offer an opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to join our Maintenance team. 
This Graduate position provides recent graduates with the opportunity to develop professional skills and experience across City of Newcastle while contributing to meaningful projects and operational activities.  
Kickstart your civil engineering career with hands-on experience across asset management, project planning and project delivery. As a Graduate Civil Engineer, you will be supported to build your technical capability while contributing to meaningful infrastructure projects and programmed maintenance activities that make a real difference across Newcastle. 
Working within the City Infrastructure directorate, you will learn from experienced professionals as you help investigate and inspect infrastructure matters, provide engineering advice, assess options and recommend practical solutions.  
You will also gain exposure to the full lifecycle of infrastructure delivery, from early planning and business cases through to project briefs, scoping, quality and contract documentation, completed works reviews and the coordination of internal and external resources across roads, drainage and structures. 
This is an exciting opportunity, as a member of our team, you won't just work for the city; you’ll co-create it. 
Find out more about your new career by viewing the position description here. 
Life at City of Newcastle (CN) 
You’ll get to experience your work up close alongside the brilliant minds of your colleagues who care for one another and the region. 
You’ll chip away at ambitious plans with a talented, passionate crew alongside you, shaping the very fabric of our community. Showing up for neighbours not shareholders. 
Every single day offers the chance to think big and act local. Planning and prioritising to achieve the most important outcomes with the community. 
You’ll add value in the moments that matter. From librarians to lifeguards, in a range of iconic places, we achieve a better Newcastle together. 
Whether we’re planning to host major events, providing essential services or supporting creative artists, it’s what we do when the cameras aren't rolling that matters most. 
And we’ll be there for you in important times in your life. We embrace flexible work arrangements to find a balance that allows us to enjoy the city we shape. 
Our focus on inclusion and respecting culture, will help you feel a deeper connection with others. You'll connect with internal communities that will help you to feel a sense of belonging and reflect the diversity of the growing region. 
You’ll do meaningful work and do it sustainably as you take ideas from plan to play, in your own backyard.
With hundreds of different roles, each person adds their uniqueness to our culture and plays their part as we head towards our 2040 vision. 
With natural assets and a focus on the environment, co-create a sustainable region with us. 
Why join CN? 
At CN, we value our employees, and their wellbeing takes priority. We encourage employees to make time for what's important and provide the benefits to enable a work life balance that allow us to enjoy the city we shape. To read more, visit here!
- 35-hour working week with flexible/hybrid work arrangements/model as well as an optional 9-day fortnight 
- 4 weeks of annual leave, 3 weeks of personal leave plus 2 additional paid public holidays 
- 17.5% annual leave loading yearly payment 
- Paid parental leave for primary carers 
- Industry leading employment conditions 
- Corporate Fitness program from as little as $18.00 per fortnight
- Access to a range of exclusive CN employee benefits programs including Novated Lease options as well as access to reward and recognition vouchers 
- Annual performance development plans and ongoing training and development opportunities 
- Leading the CN Way leadership program 
- Inclusion, Diversity & Equity (IDE) employee networks and initiatives 
- Access to Health & Wellbeing programs including an Onsite Physiotherapist and Psychology, Yoga and Mental Health Ambassador Groups 
We champion inclusion so that everyone is valued, and we encourage innovation and creativity. We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive workplace where different styles, backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are valued, encouraged, and respected. 
People with diverse lived experiences (including but not limited to, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians, people with diverse gender identities and sexualities, people from different cultural, racial, ethnic, religious and linguistic backgrounds, people with disability, carers, and veterans) are encouraged to apply. 
Don’t just work for the city, co-create it. Join and expand your career at the City of Newcastle. 
What is next? 
If you are shortlisted you will be required to attend 1 x group assessment centre for a 3-hour period to be held the week of 2nd Nov 2026.
Application Closing Date: Saturday 17 October 2026
Remuneration:  $88,889.29 + 17.5% annual leave loading yearly payment + 12% Superannuation per annum for a 35-hour week
Contact: Melissa Moore - Career Ready Advisor – 02 4974 1377
If you need any adjustments to be made to the recruitment process or if you would like to discuss any accessibility requirements, please contact recruit@ncc.nsw.gov.au for a confidential discussion.

title: Civil Survey & Design Officer - Cadet or Graduate Opportunity Available
content_text:
Civil Survey & Design Officer - Cadet or Graduate Opportunity Available - Gunnedah Shire Council 
 Skip to content. 
 Civil Survey & Design Officer - Cadet or Graduate Opportunity Available
Job No:
 GSC657 
Location:
 Gunnedah 
Employment Status:
 Full Time 
No. of Vacancies:
 1 
Closing Date:
19 Oct 2026 AEDT
 Location: Gunnedah, NSW  
 Contract Type: Full Time, 35 hours per week  
 Salary Range: Grade 6 - 15 ($1234.39 - $2046.55 per week + 12% Superannuation) 
 Application Deadline: 5:00pm, Monday 19 October 2026 
 Position Title: Survey and Design Cadet , Survey and Design Graduate ,  Survey and Design Officer ,  Senior Survey and Design Officer 
 A council truly passionate about community! 
 Gunnedah Shire Council is an integral part of the Gunnedah community, a vibrant, warm and friendly town surrounded by the expansive Liverpool Plains and framed by the Nandewar Ranges. At Gunnedah Shire Council we are committed to providing a friendly and helpful service to all stakeholders. We are dedicated to Gunnedah being a liveable and accessible community for all ages and demographics. Additionally, as a council we are proud to promote economic and business development in the region.
 We are not only invested in the people of Gunnedah, we are also heavily invested in its employees and their future careers.
 Are you looking for an opportunity to join a rapidly growing industry, gain invaluable skills and mentorship whilst also achieving a qualification in surveying and design? 
 Are you an experienced Survey and Design professional looking for your next step? 
 Gunnedah Shire Council is seeking a motivated and enthusiastic individual eager to learn and grow in the role of Survey and Design Officer .
 Our Next Civil Survey & Design Officer 
 Reporting to the Manager Engineering Services, and working closely with our team of engineers, you will be working collaboratively across Council to assist with duties including:
 collecting, recording, and interpreting survey data for investigation and design of civil works.
 producing quality designs for civil works.
 undertaking survey and set out for civil construction works.
 collecting quality control and work as executed data for civil construction works.
 For those looking to join with no prior work experience, this role has been created to bring on either a Cadet , Graduate Officer or Qualified Officer - with Salary Grade and training expectations adjusted to fit the successful candidate.
 Many of our cadets and graduate hires have obtained in demand skills, which help to form the basis of a successful career. Whilst it would be advantageous, you do not need to have previous experience and applications from school leavers are encouraged . Ideally, you will be able to demonstrate:
 Identifying, analysing and resolving problems, particularly using mathematics.
 Knowledge of civil engineering processes in construction or demonstrated willingness to learn.
 Knowledge or experience in civil design and/or surveying.
 Ensuring full compliance within the scope of the fields of Civil Design & Construction and Surveying.
 Demonstrated skills and knowledge in use of Microsoft Office applications.
 Applying interpersonal skills.
 For those with experience and applying for our Senior position, the following essential criteria must be met: 
 Diploma of Engineering or commensurate level qualifications majoring in Engineering, Construction Management or Spatial Science.
 Demonstrated experience in survey and design across multiple disciplines including road design, storm water drainage, reticulation and traffic safety.
 Demonstrated experience in using modern surveying instruments including GNSS and machine guidance for graders, including calibration and maintenance.
 High level knowledge of requisite construction standards and codes for a range of civil infrastructure including Austroads and WSAA.
 Demonstrated experience using CAD packages in particular Autocad Civil 3d, and Civil Site Design.
 Demonstrated ability to work autonomously and successfully manage multiple projects.
 Demonstrated skills and knowledge in use of Microsoft Office applications.
 Ability and continued commitment to work according to Councils' policies and Code of Conduct, with or without supervision.
 Current valid NSW Class C Drivers Licence (ongoing employment is conditional on maintaining this Licence).
 Practical experience in engineering survey, design
 Familiarity with Autocad™ or other CAD software.
 Familiarity with survey instruments.
 Familiarity with GIS software.
 Applying professional interpersonal skills.
 Developing work priorities.
 Good communication and public relations skills.
 Identifying, analysing and resolving problems.
 To view the full list of Key Responsibilities, Key Tasks, Essential and Desirable Criteria please view the Senior Survey and Design Officer Position Description Attached. 
 Why Join Gunnedah Shire Council? 
 Working at Gunnedah Shire Council offers a range of benefits, some of which include:
 Accrue a Rostered Day Off (RDO) every 3 weeks!
 Access to MyLeave - An additional 5 days of leave each year to support a healthy and flexible work-life balance. 
 Receive Long Service Leave after only 5 years!
 Receive annual award salary increases with potential for further increases during performance appraisal cycles.
 Salary packaging and salary sacrificing options available - Salary Packaging Australia
 Eligible staff can access 14 weeks of paid parental leave (or 28 weeks at half pay)!
 Professional development and career growth opportunities.
 Access to 4 weeks annual leave
 Opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the community.
 Access to employee wellbeing programs
 Active social club
 For further information regarding this role please contact Daniel Abraham , Manager Engineering Services , on 02 6740 2100 or see the Position Description 
 How to Apply 
 Please read the Position Description by clicking on the link above. It is important to read this carefully to understand what the job involves.
 No candidate will meet every single desired qualification or skill. If your experience looks a little different from what we have identified and you think you can bring value to the role, we would love to learn more about you!
 If this sounds like you, click the Apply button below, complete the application form. Please ensure you answer all questions and upload a current resume and cover letter outlining your suitability for this role, as well as any copies of relevant qualifications that support your application. The use of AI to assist with creating and formatting documents is welcomed; however, written responses should remain thoughtful and personalised, as generic or impersonal submissions may be viewed less favourably.
 Only candidates with current Australian work rights (Australian citizens, permanent residents, NZ citizens with a current passport, valid work visa) will be considered.
 Further information 
 As part of the recruitment process, suitable applicants will be required to complete pre-employment screening which may include relevant background checks, functional capacity assessment and drug and alcohol screening. Our recruitment process is primarily via system generated emails.  Please ensure your email is correct before submitting your application to avoid missing crucial updates and outcomes.
 Email notifications may include application confirmation, interview invitations, request for references, and application outcomes. Please check your email regularly, including your junk email.
 Council is an equal opportunity employer is committed to a merit-based workforce that encompasses inclusiveness and diversity in an environment of mutual respect. We invite, encourage, welcome and value candidate of all ages and from all backgrounds.
 For all enquiries regarding the application and recruitment process, please contact the People and Culture team on 02 6740 2100 or peopleandculture@gunnedah.nsw.gov.au 
 For essential workers and their families moving to Gunnedah, The Welcome Experience is a free program aimed at providing free personalised support for a range of services such as housing, education, partner job opportunities, and community connection. To learn more and register for the program please click here: The Welcome Experience | NSW Government .
apply_instructions: Apply online through the Gunnedah Shire Council applynow form (job GSC657) with resume, cover letter and copies of relevant qualifications; closes 5:00pm Monday 19 October 2026 AEDT. Role enquiries: Daniel Abraham, Manager Engineering Services, 02 6740 2100. Recruitment enquiries: People and Culture, 02 6740 2100 or peopleandculture@gunnedah.nsw.gov.au.

Please outline any skills or knowledge you possess and how you believe this would be of benefit to the role?

Outline your skills and knowledge in use of Microsoft Office applications.
What class of driver's licence do you currently hold? (options include Full Licence (Class C))
Do you hold a WHS General Construction Induction Card (White card)? Yes/No
What best describes your rights to work in Australia? (Australian Citizen / NZ Citizen / Permanent Resident / Working Visa (Unrestricted) / Working Visa (With Restrictions))
When would you be available to commence work with Gunnedah Shire Council if successful? (Immediately / 1 Week / 2 Weeks / 4 Weeks or more)

title: Intern Drafter
abstract: Support Senior Drafters and Engineers in technical drawings and CAD drafting.
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a draftsperson?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
content_text:
About the Company
Menard Oceania is a design and construct specialist geotechnical contractor offering expertise in ground improvement and reinforcement for sites with poor soils. Its treatments eliminate the need for the deep foundations traditionally used to support surface structures. Our scope includes small to large infrastructure-based solutions across a broad range of market segments for private and public stakeholders, including Transport, Dams, Ports and Coastal Infrastructure, Industrial and Commercial Buildings, Heavy Industry and Mining.
Your Role
The Intern drafting Assistant will support the senior drafting & design engineers in the preparation, modification, and coordination of civil, structural and geotechnical engineering drawings and documentation. This position provides an opportunity to develop technical drafting expertise and engineering knowledge while working within a collaborative project team.
Skills and Qualifications
- Basic knowledge of engineering drawing standards and principles.
- Basic proficiency in AutoCAD; Civil 3D experience is advantageous.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Key Attributes
- Detail-oriented with a strong focus on quality and precision.
- Eager to learn and develop technical drafting and engineering knowledge.
- Organised and capable of managing multiple tasks effectively.
- Positive team player with a proactive approach to supporting project delivery.
Training & Development 
On-the-Job Training and Development
The role provides structured on-the-job training and mentoring from experienced Senior Draft’s person and the Design Manager. The successful candidate will receive hands-on guidance in engineering drafting practices, project delivery processes, and the application of industry standards across civil, structural, and geotechnical engineering disciplines.
Salary & Benefits
Remuneration will be competitive with current market rates, depending on qualifications and experience.
Applicants must have full working rights in Australia to be considered for this position
